# DSH Studio v0.7.7

This stability and macOS polish release addresses [#5](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/5)
through [#10](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/10). It fixes dual-stack DNS false
positives in plugin catalogs, adds explicit Node runtime selection, repairs native notification and
login-item integration, and keeps terminal TUIs and dark macOS Vibrancy readable in a real window.

## Added

- **Node runtime selection.** The Environment panel lists discovered compatible runtimes and persists
  the one selected. Harness launch and npm installation planning use that choice. If a version manager
  removes it, Studio safely falls back to the newest compatible runtime instead of becoming unstartable.
- **Notification test.** Settings can request native notification access and send one explicit test
  message. The first macOS delivery registers DSH Studio with Notification Center, while background
  notifications remain controlled by the existing preferences.

## Changed and secured

- macOS autostart uses an AppleScript Login Item, so it appears in System Settings and third-party
  startup managers; login still starts Studio hidden in the tray and never starts the Harness by itself.
- The embedded terminal loads Unicode 11 cell widths and pins the TUI canvas to the full terminal
  height. PTY, ANSI colour and keyboard semantics remain unchanged.
- Dark macOS Vibrancy keeps content grounds opaque while retaining native material in the chrome, so a
  light wallpaper or inactive-window tint cannot turn dark text into an unreadable gray-on-gray surface.

## Fixed and polished

- Fixed [#5](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/5): a DNS answer containing a public address
  beside a private or special-use address no longer rejects the catalog with
  `catalog host resolved to a blocked local or special-use address`. Requests still use `no_proxy` and
  one pinned public address to prevent DNS rebinding; a host with no admissible address remains blocked.
- Added rejection coverage for documentation, shared-use and IPv4-mapped IPv6 special-use addresses.
- Fixed [#6](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/6): Unicode cell widths and bottom whitespace
  could distort full-screen terminal programs. ANSI/TUI output continues through the real PTY and xterm.
- Fixed [#7](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/7): when several Node versions were visible,
  Studio silently used the newest one. A supported runtime can now be chosen, and its path is validated
  against the discovery list before it is persisted.
- Fixed [#8](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/8): macOS had no explicit notification registration
  or diagnostic path. Enabling a preference requests permission, and the Settings test button surfaces
  native failures instead of hiding them.
- Fixed [#9](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/9): macOS autostart existed only as a LaunchAgent
  and was invisible to startup managers. It is now a visible Login Item.
- Fixed [#10](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/10): dark macOS content could mix black text
  with a gray material backdrop. Opaque dark grounds and terminal colour/layout regression coverage
  keep the interface legible.

## Install and update

All macOS users, machines with multiple Node installations, and anyone affected by catalog, terminal,
notification, autostart or dark-mode issues should upgrade. Existing profiles, plugins, workspaces,
sessions and credentials remain in place; the Node selection file records only a discovered executable
path and never installs or changes a user's Node version.

Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; in-app updates continue to require the Tauri updater signature.
Windows Authenticode and Apple Developer ID are separate OS publisher signatures and depend on credentials
configured for the release repository.
